title: The imperfect to the singular: the essential verbs

blocks.text: Finally the verb. ⁧أَعْمَلُ⁩ • work • ⁧أَسْكُنُ⁩ ... ⁧أَدْرُسُ⁩ Study: with imperfection ( ⁧المُضَارِع⁩ al-muḍāriʿ ) tell you what you usually do, what you're doing and what you're going to do shortly. In this unit learn the singular conjugation, the order of the verbal phrase and the object complement, and tell a day's work. It is the most important unit of the module: it lasts two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 32–33 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-13), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. recognize the root and form of a verb and seek its form of quote;
2. combine the verbs of the section to the singular imperfection 3, with the right vowel theme;
3. build the verbal sentence (verb + subject + complement) and use the complement accusative the subject matter;
4. ask questions with ⁧مَاذَا⁩ , ⁧أَيْنَ⁩ , ⁧مَتَى⁩ + verb;
5. describe your day and understand another person's routine;
6. write 60 words about your routine.

chapters.title: 2. The Arabic Word and the Imperfect

blocks.text: Root and form of citation. Each verb has a root of three consonants ( ⁧د ر س⁩ • to study •). In Arabic dictionaries the verb is quoted to the perfect, 3to singular male person , ⁧دَرَسَ⁩ Darasa studied it. In this course, in the vocabulary you find the imperfect ( ⁧يَدْرُسُ⁩ ) followed by the perfect: you need both. The perfect one you will study in A1-18. What the imperfect one expresses. Unfinished action: usual ( ⁧أَعْمَلُ فِي مِيلَانُو⁩ Work in Milan, currently under way ( ⁧أَشْرَبُ القَهْوَةَ الآنَ⁩ I am drinking coffee, future and near ( ⁧أَرْجِعُ غَدًا⁩ I'll be back tomorrow. The explicit future with ⁧سَـ⁩ / ⁧سَوْفَ⁩ will arrive in A2. Prefixes and suffixes of the singular. The central part ( -drus-) remains the same; change the prefix and, by female, the suffix.
She... ⁧تَدْرُسُُ⁩ ⁧تَ⁩ tadrusu

"Tu" and "Tu" are of the same shape: . ⁧تَدْرُسُ⁩ The context, the pronoun or the subject say of those who speak: ⁧أَنْتَ تَدْرُسُ⁩ / ⁧هِيَ تَدْرُسُ⁩ / . ⁧سَلْمَى تَدْرُسُ⁩ The subject pronoun does not serve: the verb contains it. ⁧أَدْرُسُ⁩ = "I study" Adding ⁧أَنَا⁩ , ⁧أَنْتَ⁩ ... only to give emphasis or contrast: ⁧أَنَا أَدْرُسُ، وَهُوَ يَعْمَلُ⁩ I study, and he works. In pause falls the final -u: adrus , yaʿmal ; end-to-ends remain -īna and the suffixed pronouns: tadrusīn(a) , uḥibbuhā .
Between the second and third consonant of the root there is a vowel that varies from verb to verb: a , u or i . It is not deduced with certainty from the perfect: you learn with the verb.
⁧يَجْلِسُ⁩ sit down, sit down ⁧أَجْلِسُجَلَسَ⁩ ⁧تَجْلِسِينَ⁩ ·

A rule of principle. Many verbs with ⁧ح⁩ , ⁧خ⁩ , ⁧ع⁩ , ⁧غ⁩ , ⁧ه⁩ or ⁧ء⁩ as second or third consonant have vowel a ( ⁧يَذْهَبُ⁩ , ⁧يَفْتَحُ⁩ , ⁧يَسْمَعُ⁩ ): the gutturals are drawn to a. But there are exceptions ( ⁧يَرْجِعُ⁩ , ⁧يَدْخُلُ⁩ ). In Anki the vowel theme is always indicated.
⁧يُحِبُّ⁩ Love, pleasure, roots ⁧ح ب ب⁩ ) belongs to another verbal form (the IV, B1) and has the prefix with u; the double consonant remains united:
⁧أُحِبُّ⁩ uḥibbu ⁧تُحِبُّ⁩ tuḥibbu ⁧تُحِبِّينَ⁩ tuḥibbīna ⁧يُحِبُّ⁩ yuḥibbu ⁧تُحِبُّ⁩ tuḥibbu

I like coffee. ⁧أُحِبُّ القَهْوَةَ⁩ : in Arabic ... I love coffee... with the coffee object complement. ⁧يَأْكُلُ⁩ "Eating": at the first person two hamzas merge into ā long: ⁧آكُلُ⁩ ākulu "Eating" is the word used for "eat." The other forms are regular: . ⁧تَأْكُلُ، تَأْكُلِينَ، يَأْكُلُ يَقْرَأُ⁩ The final hamza changes support according to the vowel surrounding it (L0-09): ⁧أَقْرَأُ، تَقْرَأُ، تَقْرَئِينَ⁩ . ⁧، يَقْرَأُ⁩ The pronunciation is regular: taqraʾīna .
A sentence beginning with the verb is a verbal phrase ( ⁧جُمْلَة فِعْلِيَّة⁩ ). The most common order in the written language is verb " subject " complement ":

The deal. The verb agrees with the subject in the genre: ⁧يَعْمَلُ كَرِيم⁩ , ⁧تَعْمَلُ سَلْمَى⁩ . With female subjects the prefix is ⁧تَ⁩ - also at 3per person. Also the subject order is correct: . ⁧كَرِيم يَعْمَلُ فِي مَرْكَزِ الشُّرْطَةِ⁩ It highlights the subject (a nominal phrase with a verb as predicate). In newspaper headlines and news the verb order prevails, subject: accustomed to look for the subject after the verb.
The object of the supplement is to the accusative ( ⁧مَنْصُوب⁩ manṣūb ): -if determined, -an indeterminate.
. ⁧أَعْرِفُ عُنْوَانَهُ⁩ aʿrifu ʿunwānahu. I know his address.

The alif of tanwīn -an is written with names without ⁧ة⁩ ( ⁧شَايًا⁩ , ⁧كِتَابًا⁩ ) and not with those in ⁧ة⁩ ( ⁧رِسَالَةً⁩ ). You know her from ⁧كَمْ⁩ ( A1-06). In pause -a falls and -an remains -an in the teaching texts: aqraʾu l-ǧarīda , tašrabu šāyan . The object pronoun is the suffix attached to the verb, equal to that of the names except for "me" (-nī): ⁧أُحِبُّهَا⁩ "I love her," ⁧أَعْرِفُهُ⁩ I know him. ⁧هَلْ تَعْرِفُنِي؟⁩ Do you know me? The complete shapes you will use in A2.

⁧مَاذَا⁩ + verb (A1-06): ⁧مَاذَا تَدْرُسُ؟⁩ What are you studying? ⁧مَاذَا تَعْمَلُ؟⁩ What do you do? / what are you doing? ⁧مَاذَا تَشْرَبِينَ؟⁩ What are you drinking?
